newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African bonds were drifting toward their best levels of the day in becalmed late afternoon trade as players grabbed their jackets and headed for the door ahead of the long-weekend.
The government's R150 gilt was last at 14.640 percent versus the intraday low of 14.620 percent and Thursday's 1415 GMT level of 14.645 pct.
The market largely ignored U.S. Treasury gains which followed an unexpected decline in the U.S Producer Price Index for May.

"It's been dead quiet ahead of the long weekend and people are checking out early. The U.S. PPI numbers helped the U.S. bonds but without dealers to do trades in this market, it's not having much effect here," noted one dealer.
The broad range of range of 14.60 percent to 14.70 percent framed over the last ten days was expected to hold into the next week with a bias to the downside after recent consolidation.
In forex dealings, the rand was gradually weakening past the 4.50 level as importers scouted for dollars after exporter supplies dried up.

"There was fairly average two-way trade between 4.4980 and 4.5020. It was pretty much mixed between importers and exporters until this afternoon where the exporters' dollars kind of ran out," said one trader.
The rand was last at 4.5010/5030 from Thursday's late price of 4.4970/5000.
In cross rate action it was ahead but under its intraday best against the yen and mark, but weaker versus sterling.
The unit was last changing hands at 25.3861/4252 yen from 25.3139/3531 late Thurssday.
It was last quoted at 0.3840/3844 marks from 0.3830/3834 marks Thursday and 7.3300/3394 on sterling from 7.3483/3577 previously.

Rand and bond dealers said their markets were likely to brush off next week's first quarter current account balance -- expected to show a 2.1 billion rand deficit from a previous shortfall of 50 million -- as long as it confirmed a year-on-year decline.
"It's a very volatile number. The inflation and reserves numbers will still be the focus for most of us," said one currency trader.

"I think the market's going to be kept in this 4.4950-4.5050 range but with the way it's closed today I wouldn't completely rule out a proper test of 4.5050 which would see us up around 4.52 to 4.53. It all depends on the Reserve Bank," he added.
South Africa's money market shortage rose to 7.876 billion rand on Thursday from 7.437 billion rand on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank said.
On the money market, three-month NCD rates were static at 16.05 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate remained pegged at between 15.45 to 15.60 percent also unchanged from Thursday.
Foreigners were net buyers of 139.27 million rands worth of South African bonds on Thursday after selling 2.05 million rands worth on Wednesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative bond market volumes soared to 37.99 billion on Thursday from 5.71 billion rand previously.
Some dealers said Thursday's turnover, which traditionally jumps due to trade settlements, was likely to have been swelled by several large asset-swap and switching deals.
South Africa's financial markets are closed on Monday for the Youth Day holiday.
-- Justin McCamish, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
